newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Korea Heavy confident of Ceylon Steel takeover.
newsitem.headline: Korea Heavy confident of Ceylon Steel takeover.

text.p: Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Co Ltd is confident of winning a 90 percent stake in Ceylon Steel Corp being privatised by Sri Lanka, a company executive of the South Korean company said on Monday.

"We have put in a bid that closed last Friday and we are pretty confident we will be able to buy the company's shares by the end of this month," Korea Heavy Executive Managing Director Shin Sang-hong told Reuters.

Sri Lankan officials said last week the government was negotiating with Korea Heavy for the state-run South Korean company's total investment of about $600 million in steel, power generation and oil refinery projects.
"We have made conceptual proposals for our investment plans and the Sri Lankan government has shown very positive response," Shin said.
"We are looking at three to four places to build a new steel plant and a feasibility study would be carried out in the next three to four months," he said.
Under a longer-term investment plan, Korea Heavy hopes to build a power plant at a cost of $150 million and an oil refinery at a cost of $350 million, Shin said.
He said the planned power plant would primarily support Korea Heavy's steel plants.
"We see oil refining a promising business in Sri Lanka which is short of supply in petroleum products," Shin said.
Korea Heavy is a leading manufacturer of steel fabrication and electricity generation facilities in South Korea.
